translationRepairs: South of Liangxiang his own officers turned on him. Fearing capture, Zhu Fu dismounted and killed his wife to flee alone. The city fell to Peng Chong. Minister Secretary Hou Ba accused him of ruining Youzhou, inventing charges against Peng Chong, wasting the army, and failing to die with honor—all capital offenses.

Southward, on reaching Liangxiang, his troop chief turned and blocked him. Fearing he could not escape, Zhu Fu dismounted and stabbed his wife to death, barely escaping with his life alone. The city fell to Peng Chong. Minister Secretary Hou Ba accused him of ruining Youzhou, inventing charges against Peng Chong, wasting the army, and failing to die with honor—all capital offenses.
南至良鄉 means arriving southward at Liangxiang, and 兵長 is singular; the original's 'south of' and plural 'officers' misread both, while the proposed text also restores 恐不得脫 and 刺殺…僅以身免.

At that time the two commanderies were rebellious and depraved; the northern province was anxious and fearful; Fu thought the Son of Heaven would surely himself lead troops to punish them, but only sent Mobile General Deng Long secretly to aid Fu.

At that time the two commanderies were rebellious and depraved; the northern province was anxious and fearful; Fu thought the Son of Heaven would surely himself lead troops to punish them, but the Son of Heaven only sent Mobile General Deng Long secretly to aid Fu.
而但遣 continues the imperial agent of 天子必自將兵討之, not Fu; the proposal's bare 'he' remains ambiguous after Fu as main-clause subject, so the Son of Heaven is named explicitly.
You and Geng Yan both rose to help found the dynasty and share its favor.
You and Geng Kuang both rose to help found the dynasty and share its favor.
耿俠遊 is Geng Kuang under his courtesy name Xiayou, not his son Geng Yan; the original misidentifies the person.
Geng Yan is humble and often speaks of his own unworthiness;
Geng Kuang is humble and often speaks of his own unworthiness;
俠遊 is the same courtesy name for Geng Kuang as in s0022; rendering it as Geng Yan is a naming error.
In the Yongping period someone with solitary words denounced Fu's affairs; Emperor Xiaozong was greatly angered and granted Fu death.
In the Yongping period someone with solitary words denounced Fu's affairs; Emperor Xianzong was greatly angered and granted Fu death.
顯宗 romanizes as Xianzong; Xiaozong would require 孝宗, which the Chinese does not have.
His ancestors were a collateral branch of Wei; they ate vegetables at Feng city and thereby took it as surname.
His ancestors were a collateral branch of Wei; they held the fief-revenues of Feng city and thereby took it as surname.
食菜馮城 is the classical fief-revenue idiom (食采), not literal vegetable-eating; the proposed literal matches the idiomatic sense already present.

He married Emperor Xiaozong's daughter the senior princess of Huojia; in youth was attendant at the palace gates; by respectful solemnity and humble restraint was acclaimed; rank reached superintendent of works.

He married Emperor Xianzong's daughter the senior princess of Huojia; in youth was attendant at the palace gates; by respectful solemnity and humble restraint was acclaimed; rank reached superintendent of works.
顯宗 is temple name Xianzong; Xiaozong is a false romanization of the same characters.
In the sixth year Emperor Xiaozong visited Lu and again acted as Commandant of the Guards.
In the sixth year Emperor Xianzong visited Lu, and Fang again acted as Commandant of the Guards.
顯宗 is Xianzong, and 復行衛尉事 resumes Feng Fang as silent subject after 顯宗幸魯; the original wrongly makes the emperor the office-holder.

At the beginning of Yongping there was Xinye merit assessor Deng Yan; as a minor marquis by imperial marriage he often attended court assembly; his bearing and gait stood out from the crowd; Emperor Xiaozong eyed him and said to those beside him: 'Does my deportment match such a man!'

顯宗 romanizes as Xianzong, not Xiaozong.
Yu Fang, a collateral descendant of Yu Yan, styled Zizhong.
Yu Fang, a collateral great-grandson of Yu Yan, styled Zizhong.
從曾孫 is specifically collateral great-grandson; 'collateral descendant' drops the generational precision the Chinese states.

巨君 is Jujun; Junju reverses the courtesy-name syllables.
